title: bug: JetBrains judges a daemon reachable by a TCP probe of 127.0.0.1 only and never parses daemon.json bindHost, so a live daemon bound to ::1 or a LAN address (--host / MOE_BIND_HOST) has its daemon.json deleted and a second daemon started on the same .moe/ (JetBrains twin of doctor's task-576e3005)
description:
Filed by defect hunt task-3488566e (11-04 #17, lane 2: the JetBrains plugin's daemon lifecycle). HEAD bb0bc17e.

PROBLEM
- moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/model/Models.kt:290-295: DaemonInfo has no bindHost field, so the plugin cannot see the bind that the daemon records for any --host / MOE_BIND_HOST other than 127.0.0.1 (docs/CONFIGURATION.md:16, root CLAUDE.md "Run").
- services/MoeDaemonSupervisor.kt:914-919: isReachable = pid alive && isPortOpen. defaultPortProbe (:1043-1047) connects to 127.0.0.1 only.
- When a live same-project daemon is bound off loopback, two paths fire:
  - ensureDaemonRunningImpl skips reuse, deletes its daemon.json (:163-166) and spawns `start --project <base>` (:180-203);
  - MoeProjectService.connect() also deletes it (services/MoeProjectService.kt:175-178).
- The daemon's own guard would have refused the duplicate. existingDaemonBlocksStart (packages/moe-daemon/src/index.ts:619-625) probes bindHost and logs "Moe daemon already running". The plugin removes daemon.json before its spawned `start` can run that guard, and the first daemon released its lock long ago (index.ts:859).
- The plugin only ever dials ws://127.0.0.1 (MoeProjectService.kt:331; docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:366), so it cannot use such a daemon anyway. The defect is destroying its discovery file and starting a second writer.

EVIDENCE: architect re-run on the bb0bc17e snapshot (port 19888, isolated HOME). The plugin's decision is mirrored, no Gradle run: /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-3488566e/mine/bindhost-rerun.txt (script: A/repro-bindhost.sh).
  daemon.json: "pid": 2056623, "bindHost": "::1"
  pid 2056623 alive=true; 127.0.0.1:19888 open=false; [::1]:19888 open=true; plugin isReachable=false
  (delete + spawn as at :163-166/:180-203) second daemon "pid": 2056776, no bindHost
  first daemon _run pid 2056623 alive: yes; [::1]:19888/health: 200; 127.0.0.1:19888/health: 200
  both /health projectPath: /tmp/hunt-3488-snap/fixtures/bindproj-mine | /tmp/hunt-3488-snap/fixtures/bindproj-mine
The daemon CLI's own guard on the same kind of record: A/repro-bindhost-daemon-guard.out shows "INFO: Moe daemon already running", and daemon.json pid unchanged.

FIX DIRECTION
- Parse bindHost (nullable).
- When the recorded pid is alive and bindHost is set and is not loopback, 0.0.0.0, :: or wsl, never delete daemon.json and never spawn. Publish a status that names the bind host: the plugin connects on 127.0.0.1 only.
- If the plugin probes bindHost at all, do so only when it is an address of a local interface (the daemon's BIND_HOST_NOT_LOCAL rule; the d6ebe4ab boundary: never dial a host that repository content names).
- Out of scope: the daemon, a relative recorded projectPath (sibling row task-78fa7110 fixes it at the daemon), the VS Code client, docs/MCP_SERVER.md.

FILES: moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/model/Models.kt, moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/services/MoeDaemonSupervisor.kt, moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/services/MoeProjectService.kt, moe-jetbrains/src/test/kotlin/com/moe/services/MoeDaemonSupervisorTest.kt (MoeProjectServiceTest.kt if the connect() path gets its own case). No open row holds any of them (lanes.js 06:50Z). The gate is `./gradlew test` under the jetbrains-gradle lease.
definitionOfDone: A JUnit case in MoeDaemonSupervisorTest.kt: daemon.json with bindHost "::1", processAliveProbe true and portProbe false. ensureDaemonRunning() returns false, processStarter is never called, daemon.json is byte-identical afterwards, and the published status names "::1".

A JUnit case proves MoeProjectService's connect() path also keeps that daemon.json (no deleteDaemonInfoIfUnchanged for a live pid with an off-loopback bindHost). A record with no bindHost, or bindHost "wsl", still behaves exactly as today, so the existing supervisor tests pass unchanged.
`./gradlew test` in moe-jetbrains (under the jetbrains-gradle lease) passes, and `grep -n bindHost moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/model/Models.kt` shows the nullable field.

implementationPlan.description:
SERVICE: connect() keeps that daemon.json too. The step-1 editor rule applies.

1. MoeProjectService.kt, connect(): at the top of the if (!daemonSupervisor.isReachable(daemonInfo)) { branch, before its deleteDaemonInfoIfUnchanged call:
   // A live daemon bound off 127.0.0.1 is out of reach, not stale. Its bind is the operator's choice: keep its daemon.json
   // and schedule no reconnect, which would only overwrite this status. Restart Daemon tries again.
   daemonSupervisor.offLoopbackBindRefusal(daemonInfo)?.let {
       connecting = false
       publishStatus(false, it)
       return
   }
   - The rest of the branch (the delete, its log line, the status and scheduleReconnect) stays byte-identical. This branch decides alone whenever ensureDaemonRunning returned before reading daemon.json: a restart in flight, an unresolved Windows tree, or a protected replacement in flight. Without the guard it would delete the file the supervisor just kept.
   - Scheduling no retry follows the selectionRefusal precedent a few lines above.
   - connectWithRetry is unchanged: it runs only after this plugin spawned a daemon, and it deletes nothing.

2. MoeProjectForeignDaemonTest.kt: add two tests. This file already has the fixture a connect() case needs: a temp project, the service's status listener, and the daemonSupervisor injection used by `connect and readiness retry reach health without probing an other-side pid`. MoeProjectServiceTest's fake project has no basePath, so it is not used. Inject MoeDaemonSupervisor(f.basePath, "Test", portProbe = { _, _ -> false }, processAliveProbe = ..., processStarter = ...) through the daemonSupervisor field, exactly as that test does.
   - `BH4 connect keeps a live off-loopback daemon's json, starts nothing and schedules no reconnect` (DoD 2). Write Gson().toJson(f.writeDaemonJson("S1").copy(bindHost = "::1")) to f.daemonJson; before = its text. Use processAliveProbe = { it == 4242 } and a processStarter that counts its calls and throws. Call f.service.connect(). Assert: the daemon.json text equals before; there were 0 starts; some status contains "::1" and "127.0.0.1"; the reconnectFuture field is null; the wsClient field is null; f.assertNoWebSocketRequest().
   - `BH5 connect's own stale check removes every record but a live off-loopback one`. Rows (bindHost, alive, kept): ("::1", true, true), (null, true, false), ("wsl", true, false), ("::1", false, false), each in its own withFixture. Before connect(), set the injected supervisor's private windowsRestartInFlight AtomicBoolean to true by reflection. Write the FQN java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicBoolean and add no import. ensureDaemonRunning then returns before it reads daemon.json, so connect()'s own branch decides alone. Assert per row: when kept, the text equals before, else the file is gone; f.statuses.any { "::1" in it } == kept; (reconnectFuture == null) == kept.

- A planted bindHost plus any live pid (1, or the IDE's own) now parks the plugin with this status instead of replacing the daemon, and the plugin signals nothing by itself. Recovery is the explicit Restart Daemon, whose signaling rules this task does not change. Say so in the handoff.

implementationPlan.note:
Adversarial self-review of the five-file diff, read once as a daemon.json author and once as a --host user. No code change, so step 3's gate output stands.
(1) bindHost is only compared, logged and shown; it is never dialed or resolved.
(2) The status text goes to MoeToolWindowPanel.styleStatusLabel as plain JLabel.text and starts with fixed words, so it can never render as HTML.
(3) An other-side record never reaches isProcessAlive (BH3, mutant b).
(4) Every existing deleter still fires for no, empty or loopback-serving bindHost, a dead pid, pid 0 and another project's record (BH2, BH5, unchanged suites, mutants a/c/g).
(5) A planted bindHost plus a live pid now parks the plugin with the status, and the plugin signals nothing by itself. Recovery is Restart Daemon, whose unchanged LEGACY branch still best-effort signals a live recorded pid. The status tells the user to stop the daemon first.
(6) An array or object bindHost makes the Gson parse fail (JsonSyntaxException, caught), so the record reads as absent: no delete, the spawned start runs the daemon's own guard on the intact file, and connect() deletes nothing. Before this change Gson skipped the unknown field.
(7) In production the same refusal is published twice (supervisor onStatus, then connect()). This is harmless.
(8) A pid reused after a --host daemon crashed also parks until Restart Daemon, which is inherent in keeping a record whose pid is alive.
Details are in the Serena handoff task-task-fe8111309de04ddd92e109144b50a228-handoff. I also updated decision-daemon-cli-bindhost-local-rule.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: When .moe/daemon.json names this project, records a bindHost that does not serve 127.0.0.1 (anything but absent, empty, 127.0.0.1, 0.0.0.0, :: or wsl), comes from this side of the WSL boundary, and names a positive pid that is alive, the JetBrains plugin keeps that daemon.json byte for byte, starts no daemon, and publishes a status naming the bind host and 127.0.0.1. Both ensureDaemonRunning and connect() do this, and connect() then schedules no reconnect. Every other record is handled exactly as before.
acceptanceCriteria: BH1: a live same-project record with bindHost ::1 (also 192.0.2.10, localhost, 127.0.0.2), processAliveProbe true and portProbe false: ensureDaemonRunning() returns false, processStarter is never called, the bytes are unchanged, and one status names the host and 127.0.0.1.
BH2: no bindHost, empty, wsl, 0.0.0.0, ::, 127.0.0.1, a dead pid and pid 0 are each deleted and spawned as today, with no status.
BH3: an other-side record with bindHost ::1 never has its pid probed and behaves as the existing other-side test does.
BH4: MoeProjectService.connect() keeps that record's daemon.json, starts nothing, publishes the status and schedules no reconnect.
BH5: with ensureDaemonRunning short-circuited, connect()'s own branch keeps only the live off-loopback record, and removes and reconnects for no bindHost, wsl and a dead pid.
The full plugin suite passes with every existing test unchanged, and Models.kt shows the nullable bindHost.

A pid from an other-side record is never probed: isOtherSideOfWsl is checked before isProcessAlive.

deleteDaemonInfoIfUnchanged's data-class equality now also covers bindHost.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: 1) Probe bindHost's /health when it names a local interface (the daemon's isLocalAddress rule). Rejected: the plugin dials ws://127.0.0.1 only, so a successful probe could not be used. A Kotlin port of isLocalAddress (interface reads, zones, IPv4-mapped forms) would also be new attack surface for no gain. 2) Keep daemon.json but still spawn `start`, and let the daemon's existingDaemonBlocksStart refuse the duplicate. Rejected: DoD 1 says processStarter is never called, and the plugin's spawn/poll/kill loop would hide the explanation. 3) scheduleReconnect after the refusal. Rejected: every retry publishes 'Reconnecting... (n/10)' over the status. The bind is the operator's choice, and connect() already skips the retry for selectionRefusal. 4) Apply the guard to other-side records. Rejected: their pid is in another namespace and is never probed. Keyed on bindHost alone, the guard would wedge a dead other-side record forever, because Restart Daemon refuses other-side metadata.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: The daemon records bindHost only when host !== '127.0.0.1' (packages/moe-daemon/src/index.ts:849). probeHostFor maps '0.0.0.0', '::' and 'wsl' to 127.0.0.1 (packages/moe-daemon/src/server/probeHost.ts:17-19), so those binds answer where the plugin dials and keep today's path. Every other recorded value means 127.0.0.1 may be closed while the daemon lives: ::1, 127.0.0.2, localhost, a LAN address or a name. The guard runs only after isReachable failed, so a bind that does serve 127.0.0.1 never reaches it. ensureDaemonRunning has one caller, MoeProjectService.connect(). Gson builds DaemonInfo without its constructor (Unsafe allocation), so a missing bindHost is null. It omits null fields when writing, so existing test fixtures write the same bytes. Kotlin backtick test names cannot contain '.' or ':'.
planningNotes.risks: A test name with '::1' or an IP will not compile (mem:gotcha-kotlin-test-names-no-dot). isReachable probes the pid before the guard does, so BH1 must not assert an exact probe list. The guard order matters: a pid probe before the other-side check probes a foreign namespace (BH3 catches it). A JSON array or object bindHost now fails the whole parse; it reads as absent, as any malformed field already does. The status text must start with fixed words. The architect could not run Gradle (no lease for the architect role), so the worker's first gated run is the first compile: keep the spelled-out names, and fix only syntax if the compiler disagrees. Out of scope, unchanged: the VS Code client (no bindHost handling there either), the daemon, docs (no doc describes the old delete-and-spawn behavior), connectWithRetry, and restartDaemon's post-stop delete.
